actions.justification: MANDATORY - ABCs take priority in all poisoned patients per toxicology guidelines. Must be completed first to ensure patient stability.
MANDATORY - Vital sign assessment is required at initial presentation to identify hemodynamic instability or toxidrome features.
MANDATORY - Identifying the toxidrome guides antidote selection and treatment. Critical for intentional ingestion workup.
MANDATORY: Must identify the substance ingested, amount, time of ingestion, and route to guide all subsequent management. This is the cornerstone of toxicology assessment for intentional ingestion.
Continuous cardiac and pulse oximetry monitoring is indicated for all intentional ingestions to detect early deterioration, arrhythmias, or hemodynamic instability before the toxin is identified.
Rapid bedside glucose check is essential in all intentional ingestions as hypoglycemia can mimic or complicate toxidromes and requires immediate correction.

MANDATORY action: Guidelines require assessment of decontamination indication (e.g., activated charcoal within 1-2 hours if airway protected and no caustic ingestion). Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
Poison control should be contacted for all intentional ingestions to guide management, identify specific toxin, and recommend targeted interventions.
Anion gap calculation is part of standard toxicological workup to identify metabolic acidosis patterns (e.g., salicylate, methanol, ethylene glycol, or other toxic ingestions).
Mandatory action: provide supportive care for intentional ingestion patient. ABCs have been assessed; supportive care is the cornerstone of toxicology management.
Mandatory action: reassess clinical status to identify any evolving toxidrome or deterioration. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
IV access is essential for intentional ingestion to enable rapid medication/antidote administration, fluid resuscitation, and lab draws per toxicology guidelines.

Mandatory action: determine appropriate disposition for this intentional ingestion patient. Guidelines require all intentional ingestions to have psychiatric evaluation before discharge and observation duration based on toxin kinetics.

Mandatory action: serial lab monitoring required per toxicology guidelines to trend pending labs and detect evolving toxicity. Key labs including acetaminophen and salicylate levels must be monitored in all intentional ingestions.

Mandatory action: serial vital sign monitoring required to detect hemodynamic changes or developing toxidrome. Patient currently stable but continuous reassessment is essential in intentional ingestion scenarios.
Osmolar gap calculation helps identify toxic alcohols or other osmotically active substances in intentional ingestions, aiding toxin identification when the ingested substance is unknown.

Pending identification of the specific toxin from labs (acetaminophen/salicylate levels are key per guideline for all intentional ingestions). If acetaminophen toxicity is confirmed, N-acetylcysteine is indicated. This action should be staged pending lab confirmation.

Patient presented with intentional ingestion. At 85 minutes post-arrival, activated charcoal may still be beneficial if ingestion was within 1-2 hours and airway is protected (SpO2 98%, stable vitals). Guideline supports single-dose activated charcoal if <1-2 hours post-ingestion with protected airway, unless caustic ingestion is confirmed (which has not been established here).

All intentional ingestions require observation (4-6 hours for immediate-release, 12-24 hours for sustained-release) and psychiatric evaluation before discharge per guideline. Admit to observation to facilitate monitoring and mandatory psychiatric evaluation.
